input.command: ls -R src | head -50; cat -n src/config.ts; grep -rn "ADMIN_CIDR\|auditLog" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules
input.description: List source files and show config

input.command: cat -n src/routes.ts; grep -rn "isAdminAddress\|routes\|auditLog" src; git log --oneline | head; git show --stat HEAD | head -30
grep -rn "buildRoutes\|audit" src; ls; cat -n src/api.ts | head -60

input.reason: In src/config.ts, line 3 sets ADMIN_CIDR = "0.0.0.0/0", and isAdminAddress (line 6) calls cidrContains with that value. In cidrContains (line 12), a prefix length of 0 makes mask = 0. Line 13 then computes (toInt(base) & 0) === (toInt(ip) & 0), which is 0 === 0, so it returns true for every input. That includes non-IPv4 strings such as IPv6 addresses: toInt returns NaN for them, and NaN & 0 is 0. The only access control in routes.ts auditLog (line 43) is `if (!isAdminAddress(req.ip)) return { status: 403 }`. That check can never fail, so the handler always reads and returns AUDIT_LOG. auditLog does not check req.user or any role, and I found no other guard in the repo. I could not see how buildRoutes is mounted or whether some upstream auth exists, because nothing in the repo mounts it. Even so, the IP allowlist, which is the handler's only admin check, is a no-op as written.
input.failure_scenario: A client from any address, for example req.ip = "203.0.113.7" from the public internet, calls the auditLog route. isAdminAddress("203.0.113.7") computes mask 0, so (0 & 0) === (anything & 0) and it returns true. The 403 branch is skipped, and the handler returns the full contents of /var/harbor/audit.log with status 200. Non-admin callers can read the audit log.
input.severity_reason: The only admin check on auditLog (src/routes.ts:43) always passes, so any caller that reaches the route gets the sensitive audit log. I rated this High, not Critical, because the repo does not show how the routes are mounted or whether some upstream authentication limits who can reach them.
